summary:
S.J. Res. 163, introduced by Senator Merkley on April 13, 2026, is a privileged joint resolution invoking Congress's war powers to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Section 1 sets forth congressional findings, including that Congress holds the sole power to declare war under Article I, Section 8, Clause 11; that Congress has neither declared war on Iran nor enacted a specific statutory authorization for the use of military force within or against Iran; and that such use of force constitutes the introduction of Armed Forces into hostilities within the meaning of section 4(a) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1543(a)). The findings further characterize the resolution as one qualifying for expedited (privileged) floor consideration pursuant to section 1013 of the Department of State Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1984 and 1985 (50 U.S.C. 1546a), which incorporates the expedited procedures of section 601(b) of the International Security Assistance and Arms Export Control Act of 1976 (Pub. L. 94-329).

Section 2(a) is the operative directive. Pursuant to 50 U.S.C. 1546a and section 601(b) of the 1976 Act, Congress directs the President to remove the Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran unless such hostilities are explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force. The provision does not amend the U.S. Code; it operates as a stand-alone congressional directive under the War Powers framework and does not specify a removal deadline within its own text (the underlying statutory procedures supply the timing and expedited-consideration mechanism).

Section 2(b) supplies a rule of construction providing that nothing in the section may be construed to prevent the United States from: (1) defending against an attack on the United States or its personnel or facilities in other nations; (2) collecting, analyzing, or sharing intelligence—including with partner countries attacked by Iran since February 28, 2026, and other nations and international organizations—related to defense from threats from Iran or its proxies; or (3) assisting partner countries attacked by Iran since February 28, 2026, and other nations by intercepting retaliatory attacks on their territory by Iran or its proxies, or by providing defensive materiel support for such defensive measures.

The resolution contains no authorization of appropriations, no sunset provision, and no separate effective-date clause. It was read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
